title: person_tombstone_publish_queue semantics: given_up_at rows are Postgres-deleted but maybe live in ClickHouse
answers: Why does a deleted person still show in analytics?
What does given_up_at mean in person_tombstone_publish_queue?
How are persons stuck between Postgres tombstone and ClickHouse tracked?
body:
`person_tombstone_publish_queue` (rust/persons_migrations/20260923000001_add_person_tombstone_publish_queue.sql) is keyed by `(team_id, person_uuid)` and holds `person_version`, retry bookkeeping (`attempts`, `last_attempt_at`, `last_error`) and `given_up_at`.
- Row present = person tombstoned in Postgres by DeletePersons, ClickHouse tombstone not yet confirmed.
- `given_up_at` set = sweeper stopped retrying; person is deleted in PG but possibly still live in ClickHouse (operator work list).
- Partial index `person_tombstone_publish_queue_pending` on `tombstoned_at WHERE given_up_at IS NULL` serves the retry sweep; queries for pending rows should filter on `given_up_at IS NULL` to use it.
- Planned design: the replica inserts the row in the same transaction as the tombstone (with PERSON_DELETE_TOMBSTONE on); a Dagster sweeper deletes rows once ClickHouse shows the tombstone. Not yet wired in this PR.
applies: Code that writes/reads the tombstone queue (personhog-replica DeletePersons, Dagster sweeper).
says: Deleted person still appears in customer analytics reports
